output.subject: Your closing cashier's check from the Bridge St branch
output.body:
Dear ⟦CUSTOMER_NAME_1⟧,

Thank you for writing to us about the cashier's check you received after closing your savings account.

You told us that you closed the account at our Bridge St branch on August 17, and that the cashier's check for your balance of $846.10 arrived in the mail made out to a name that is not spelled the way your name is spelled. You mentioned that your other bank will not accept the check because of the name, so you have not been able to deposit your funds. You also let us know that the branch told you they need to research the matter before a new check can be issued, and you have asked us to send a replacement check with your name spelled correctly.

We understand how frustrating it is to wait for your own funds and then find you cannot use them. We're sorry for the inconvenience this has caused.

Our Deposit Operations team will review your complaint and your request, and we will respond to you within 10 business days.

Kind regards,

Customer Care, Meridian Harbor Bank
notes_for_analyst: Greeting token is the name the customer says was misspelled on the check; confirm the correct spelling before sending.
Customer's correct name is given in the complaint; verify it against account records before any reissue.
Decide whether and how the $846.10 check will be reissued, and the timing.
Check the status of the branch research at Bridge St and whether the original check must be returned or voided.
Confirm the account closure date of Aug 17 and the closing balance.
Customer signed as 'S.' with a surname token; check whether the account holder name on file matches.
